---
title: "Questions"
---

## Projects

<details class="q" id="is-there-a-project-in-the-course"><summary>Is there a project component in the course?</summary>

Yes and no. Each assignment has a project-like question, the same for all students, so it is a more structured project. There is no separate project component: we feel this gives you a better understanding of the concepts, and the added structure helps you get started.

</details>

<details class="q" id="what-does-a-project-question-look-like"><summary>Can you give an example of a project question?</summary>

An activity classifier (walking, running and so on). We start with publicly available datasets, then help you collect your own data with a smartphone and build a classifier on it. Those who want to go beyond the learning objectives can deploy the classifier on their smartphone.

</details>

## Prerequisites

<details class="q" id="what-are-the-prerequisites"><summary>What are the course prerequisites?</summary>

Like all courses at IIT Gandhinagar, there are no formal prerequisites, but you are assumed to have a basic understanding of:

- programming in Python, and data structures (ES 242 or equivalent)
- probability and statistics
- linear algebra
- calculus

</details>

<details class="q" id="what-is-the-prerequisite-exam"><summary>What is the prerequisite exam?</summary>

An [exam](exams/prereq.qmd) designed to make sure you have the background needed for the course.

</details>

<details class="q" id="how-do-i-prepare-for-the-prerequisite-exam"><summary>How can I prepare for the prerequisite exam?</summary>

Your undergraduate course material should be enough. You can also use the preparation material listed under [References](index.qmd#references) on the home page.

</details>

<details class="q" id="what-if-i-do-not-clear-the-prerequisite-exam"><summary>What happens if I do not clear the prerequisite exam?</summary>

You will not be allowed to take the course.

</details>

<details class="q" id="what-does-clear-the-exam-mean"><summary>What does it mean to clear the exam?</summary>

As in all courses at IIT Gandhinagar, the instructor decides the cut-off, and you must score above it. The cut-off is not revealed in advance.

</details>

## Laptop policy

<details class="q" id="can-i-use-my-laptop-in-class"><summary>Can I use my laptop in class?</summary>

No. Laptops are not allowed in class for any reason.

</details>

## Quizzes

<details class="q" id="what-if-i-miss-a-quiz"><summary>What happens if I miss a quiz for any reason?</summary>

The quiz is marked zero. Counting the best three of four quizzes is designed for such cases.

</details>

<details class="q" id="are-quizzes-open-book"><summary>Are the quizzes and exams open book? Can I bring notes?</summary>

No. Quizzes and exams are closed book, and notes are not permitted.

</details>

<details class="q" id="when-are-answer-sheets-returned"><summary>How soon will I get my answer sheets back?</summary>

Within four to five working days.

</details>

<details class="q" id="is-there-a-mid-or-end-semester-exam"><summary>Is there a mid-semester or end-semester exam?</summary>

Two of the four quizzes are held in the mid-semester and end-semester exam slots. The other two are held during the semester.

</details>

<details class="q" id="quiz-format"><summary>Are the quizzes multiple choice or written?</summary>

They may contain both multiple-choice and written questions.

</details>

## Assignments

<details class="q" id="what-if-i-miss-an-assignment"><summary>What happens if I miss an assignment deadline?</summary>

There are no extensions for assignments.

</details>

<details class="q" id="whom-do-i-ask-about-an-assignment"><summary>I have a doubt about an assignment. Whom should I ask?</summary>

Ask on the #assignments channel on Slack. If you do not get a reply within two days, write to the instructor.

</details>

<details class="q" id="can-i-use-another-language"><summary>I do not know Python. Can I write assignments in another language?</summary>

No. Assignments must be written in Python.

</details>

<details class="q" id="how-are-assignments-evaluated"><summary>How are assignments evaluated?</summary>

Each assignment is followed by a viva. The TAs first check that the code matches your submission; any change from the submitted code draws a warning. They then run the code and ask a few questions: about 75% on the assignment itself and about 25% on the theory behind it.

The marks are split as follows:

- the code runs correctly and solves the problem: 50%
- questions on the assignment and your understanding of the code: 25%
- code quality: 12.5%
- questions on the theory behind the assignment: 12.5%

</details>

<details class="q" id="individual-or-group"><summary>Are assignments individual or in groups?</summary>

In groups. All members of a group get the same grade.

</details>

## Attendance

<details class="q" id="attendance-policy"><summary>What is the attendance policy?</summary>

See [Attendance](assessment.qmd#attendance) under Assessment.

</details>

## Auditing

<details class="q" id="audit-policy"><summary>Can I audit the course?</summary>

You are free to attend the lectures. With a limited number of TAs and many students, we cannot grade your submissions, and you cannot formally contribute to a team's assignments.

</details>

## Computing resources

<details class="q" id="computational-resources"><summary>Will I get computing resources?</summary>

Typically the course has been given Google Cloud credits, which are more than sufficient for the assignments. This section will be updated once the credits are available.

</details>
